subject: ENG
label: Grade 06
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 06 English, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 7 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Reading prose and drama
modules.outcome: identify theme, character and point of view with evidence
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Reading prose and drama', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: identify theme, character and point of view with evidence. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Reading prose and drama' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: identify theme, character and point of view with evidence, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Main idea in one sentence. Character: what they say and do shows what they are like (she gave away her lunch: generous). Drama: names on the left, stage directions in brackets. Method: Model run for 'Reading prose and drama'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Identify theme, character and point of view with evidence: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.

modules.title: Pronouns, tenses and sentence types
modules.outcome: use pronouns, tenses and four sentence types accurately
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Pronouns, tenses and sentence types', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: use pronouns, tenses and four sentence types accurately. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.

modules.example: Solved: In 'Mira has a dog called Bruno', 'dog' is a common noun, 'Mira' and 'Bruno' are proper nouns and need capital letters. Method: Model run for 'Pronouns, tenses and sentence types'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. modules.standard: Use pronouns, tenses and four sentence types accurately: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Choose the right pronoun. Subject: I, he, she, we, they. Object: me, him, her, us, them. Model: "She gave him the book." "Between you and me, it was easy." Reason: use object forms after verbs and prepositions.

Step 2, Match the tense to the time. Present: "She studies every night." Past: "She studied last night." Present perfect: "She has studied for an hour." Future: "She will study tomorrow." Reason: the time word guides the tense.

Step 3, Use the four sentence types. Statement: "The library opens at nine." Question: "When does it open?" Command: "Please close the door." Exclamation: "What a lovely surprise!" Reason: each type has a purpose and punctuation.
Step 4, Check subject-verb agreement. "The team plays well." "The boys play well." "Neither of the answers is correct." Reason: the verb agrees with the subject, not the nearest noun.
Step 5, Fix an error. Wrong: "Me and her goes to the market." Right: "She and I go to the market." Another error: "He have finished his work." Right: "He has finished his work."

Step 6, Rewrite a paragraph with consistent tense. Before: "Yesterday, I walk to school and see my friend." After: "Yesterday, I walked to school and saw my friend." Underline the verbs to check them.

Step 7, Your turn. Write one sentence of each type about a school trip. Model answer: "We visited the museum." "What did you see there?" "Please bring your notebook." "How amazing the dinosaurs were!"

Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. modules.standard: Present a short talk and give feedback: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Plan the talk in minutes. Topic: "A book I recommend". Opening: 30 seconds. Main points: two minutes. Close: 30 seconds. Reason: planning time keeps you from rushing or running out.

Step 2, Write an opening that catches attention. "Have you ever read a story that you could not put down? Today I want to tell you about one." Reason: a question or a surprising fact draws the audience in.
Step 3, Use short cue cards. Card: "Title; main character; one exciting moment; why I recommend it." Reason: cards hold prompts, not the full script, so your voice stays natural.

Step 4, Give feedback with a model. Use: two stars and a wish. "Your voice was clear and the examples were interesting. Next time, slow down a little." Reason: praise first, then one specific suggestion, is useful and kind.

Step 5, Fix an error. Weak feedback: "It was fine." Better: "I liked how you described the main character. Your ending was clear." Another error: criticising the speaker. Right: describe what you saw or heard.

Step 6, Close the talk and invite a reply. "To sum up, this story is exciting and thoughtful, so I recommend it. Thank you. Any questions?" Reason: ending with a summary and thanks tells the audience you are done.

Step 7, Your turn. Write the opening line and a two stars and a wish feedback for a classmate's talk on football. Model answer: "Opening: What makes a team win? Feedback: Clear voice, good facts. Next time, look at the audience more."

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Reading prose and drama), and at which Bloom level is it?
'identify', at the Remember level.
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 7 (Speaking and listening) run?
Weeks 34 to 36.
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A worked task and a corrected copy. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
